real_estate.homebuilder: Boomers hold 41% of America's home value, and half of our local owner homes have a householder 55 or older.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates eased a little. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.32%, down 0.02, with the 15-year at 6.87%. On today's $1,199,999 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $6,595 a month in principal and interest.

Who owns America's real estate? The Federal Reserve's latest data, for the second quarter of 2026, puts the value of homes owned and lived in by households at $49.8 trillion, and Baby Boomers hold $20.5 trillion of it, 41.3% (chart). Gen X holds 28.7%, Millennials and younger 22.4% (up from 11.5% at the end of 2019), and the Silent generation 7.6%. The version going around uses the fourth quarter of 2025; the Fed has published two quarters since.

Locally the Census Bureau counts homes rather than dollars (chart). Averaging 2020 to 2024, about 31,700 of the 115,000 owner-occupied homes in our five cities had a householder 65 or older, and about 58,000, roughly half, had one 55 or older. Union City runs oldest at 31.6% aged 65 or older, then Hayward 30.3%, Milpitas 26.5%, Fremont 25.9% and Newark 22.8%, all below the national 33.0%.

That handoff is already showing up. Cotality data, as reported by Sherwood News in March, put inherited homes at about 17.5% of California property transfers in 2025, a record and about double the rate in the rest of the country. Some heirs move in, some rent, and some list.

Tuesday's export shows 2,207 board wide, from 2,244 Monday, with 132 coming soon and 79 brand new. The five city ledger is 562, from 560 Monday: Fremont (195), Hayward (162) and Union City (54) each added one, Milpitas (84) lost one, and Newark (67) held.

What this means for you: owners 55 and older can carry their property tax base to a replacement home anywhere in California under Prop. 19, up to three times, which can make a downsize pencil. Families inheriting a home should know Prop. 19 also narrowed the parent to child tax break. Run the numbers with a tax professional before deciding to keep or sell.

• Board wide: 2,207 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 132 coming soon and 79 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 562 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 492 are on the market and 70 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 195 live, 159 active, 26 coming soon and 8 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,199,999 at $782 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 41 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 162, Milpitas 84, Newark 67, Union City 54.
• Across all five cities the median is $999,894 at $668 a square foot. 249 homes are priced under a million, and 190 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Cards are Tuesday's close against Monday's.
stocks.news:
Monday's tech rally ran out of room. The Nasdaq fell 1.48% and the S&P 500 0.50%, while the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, back above 50,000 for the first time since Nov. 18. The chips that led Monday led the way back down: Nvidia, up 31.5% Monday after its board reinstated Jensen Huang, fell 5.86% to $155.38, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index lost 7.88%, with Micron down 11.01% and AMD 8.86%. Anthropic fell 6.54% to $81.91, below its $83 offering price.

Nvidia's year has been a ride (chart). It closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6, fell to $125.53 on Nov. 20 while Huang was out, and Monday's close of $165.05 left it 11.5% below where it started the year. Tuesday's close leaves it 16.7% below.

Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday's session ends early, at 10 a.m. Pacific. Rollercoasters are more fun to watch than to ride.

economy.note: The 10-Year is Treasury's official Tuesday close. Gold and silver are Tuesday's December COMEX settlements. Brent is Monday's ICE settlement (January), the latest from our locked source.
economy.commentary:
Rate hike bets are back. Futures pricing cited by Yahoo Finance on Tuesday put the odds of a quarter point Fed hike at the Dec. 8 to 9 meeting at about 95%, with the other 5% on a half point move, as Monday's AI rally stirred inflation worries again. The 10-year Treasury closed at 4.91%, down 0.01 point.

Metals gave back Monday's bounce. Gold settled at $3,561.90, down 2.45%, and silver at $40.78, down 5.54%. Brent settled Monday at $89.37, down 3.46% from Friday.

A holiday week will not stop the rate debate. It only shortens the trading hours for it.

crypto.commentary:
Bitcoin held just under $60,000. It was near $59,984 at 2:40 PM PT, down 1.88% over 24 hours on CoinGecko, after seven straight weekly losses. Ether was near $1,684.73 (-1.47%) and XRP near $0.92 (-1.35%).

Crypto followed tech lower again. It has not followed it higher in a while.
